questions.article: Ramadan: A Month of Rigorous Training
questions.q: Patience and God-consciousness are needed all year. Why, then, does the article call Ramadan a “crash course”?
options: Because its lessons are forgotten quickly
Not quite. The article says: For one month a strict discipline trains these qualities so that they stay part of one’s character the rest of the year.
Because only beginners need it
Not quite. The article says: For one month a strict discipline trains these qualities so that they stay part of one’s character the rest of the year.
Because the month is shorter than others
Not quite. The article says: For one month a strict discipline trains these qualities so that they stay part of one’s character the rest of the year.
For one month a strict discipline trains these qualities so that they stay part of one’s character the rest of the year
Yes. Practice in refraining even from what one wants.
questions.rationale: “For one month, certain habits are enforced as part of a certain discipline, so that for the rest of the year, the person will have no difficulty in exercising the same control over all of their actions.”

questions.q: A researcher is quoted: “The human brain is very resilient. Give it a chance and it will make every effort to repair itself.” How does the article say one gives it that chance?
options: By talking the matter over repeatedly
Not quite. The article says: By keeping patient and calm after a setback, not disturbing the natural process of recovery.
By working harder at once
Not quite. The article says: By keeping patient and calm after a setback, not disturbing the natural process of recovery.
By keeping patient and calm after a setback, not disturbing the natural process of recovery
Well read. Resilience is a law of nature.
By changing one’s surroundings
Not quite. The article says: By keeping patient and calm after a setback, not disturbing the natural process of recovery.
questions.rationale: “When you suffer some kind of damage either internally or externally, keep your patience. Be empty-minded for a while.”

questions.q: The body’s many organs work together without our effort. What does the article ask us to draw from this?
options: Gratitude to the Creator, which keeps one from complaint and makes one a positive thinker
Right. “To breathe is a luxury.”
Pride in the human body
Not quite. The article says: Gratitude to the Creator, which keeps one from complaint and makes one a positive thinker.
Indifference, since it happens by itself
Not quite. The article says: Gratitude to the Creator, which keeps one from complaint and makes one a positive thinker.
Worry about possible illness
Not quite. The article says: Gratitude to the Creator, which keeps one from complaint and makes one a positive thinker.
questions.rationale: “This realization makes us conscious of great blessings of the Creator… Hence, we should cultivate a feeling of gratitude for the Creator.”

questions.q: What did Caliph Umar say of a man he had liked, on learning that the man did no work?
options: That the man lost his worth in Umar’s eyes
Yes. Idleness wastes one’s best gifts.
That work is not for everyone
Not quite. The article says: That the man lost his worth in Umar’s eyes.
That he should be given a pension
Not quite. The article says: That the man lost his worth in Umar’s eyes.
That the man was fortunate to be free
Not quite. The article says: That the man lost his worth in Umar’s eyes.
questions.rationale: “On learning that he does not work, he appears to me of no value.”

questions.q: What does the article advise for someone who has no financial need to work?
options: To travel constantly
Not quite. The article says: To occupy himself with higher aims and worthy causes rather than slip into idleness.
To enjoy his leisure fully
Not quite. The article says: To occupy himself with higher aims and worthy causes rather than slip into idleness.
To give away all he owns
Not quite. The article says: To occupy himself with higher aims and worthy causes rather than slip into idleness.
To occupy himself with higher aims and worthy causes rather than slip into idleness
Well reasoned. A life without commitment decays.
questions.rationale: “If one is financially independent, one should turn one’s attention to higher things, pursue noble ends, serve worthy causes and keep oneself fruitfully occupied every day.”

questions.q: “If you persevere and fear God, their designs will never harm you in the least” (3:120). How does the article explain this in natural terms?
options: Patience and humility bring an opponent back to a normal state, where his own conscience restrains him
Correct. It is against human nature to oppose what is plainly right.
Opponents grow tired with time
Not quite. The article says: Patience and humility bring an opponent back to a normal state, where his own conscience restrains him.
Hardship makes one physically stronger
Not quite. The article says: Patience and humility bring an opponent back to a normal state, where his own conscience restrains him.
Others will come to one’s defence
Not quite. The article says: Patience and humility bring an opponent back to a normal state, where his own conscience restrains him.
questions.rationale: “Adherence to the path of patience… and piety… form the best formula to bring an antagonist back to a reasonable frame of mind.”

questions.q: The article distinguishes inner spirituality from “applied” spirituality. What is the latter?
options: Spiritual values shown in dealings with others – peaceful adjustment, turning negative into positive
Right. The inner must reach the outer.
Spirituality practised only in solitude
Not quite. The article says: Spiritual values shown in dealings with others – peaceful adjustment, turning negative into positive.
Spirituality taught in classrooms
Not quite. The article says: Spiritual values shown in dealings with others – peaceful adjustment, turning negative into positive.
Spirituality measured by ritual
Not quite. The article says: Spiritual values shown in dealings with others – peaceful adjustment, turning negative into positive.
questions.rationale: “A person’s spirituality must impinge on his environment. His elevated spiritual values must become evident in his dealings with others.”

questions.q: A man asked whether care was needed even in using water. What did the Prophet reply?
options: “Water is plentiful; use it freely”
Not quite. The article says: “Yes, do not waste water, even if you are on the banks of a flowing river”.
“Only when others are watching”
Not quite. The article says: “Yes, do not waste water, even if you are on the banks of a flowing river”.
“Yes, do not waste water, even if you are on the banks of a flowing river”
Yes. Gratitude shows itself in care.
“Only when water is scarce”
Not quite. The article says: “Yes, do not waste water, even if you are on the banks of a flowing river”.
questions.rationale: “The Prophet replied: ‘Yes, do not waste water, even if you are on the banks of a flowing river.’”

questions.q: Most bodily functions are run by the unconscious mind. What does the article say this frees the conscious mind to do?
options: To seek the truth – the purpose and meaning of life
Exactly. “Think, think and think!”
To supervise the body more closely
Not quite. The article says: To seek the truth – the purpose and meaning of life.
To entertain itself
Not quite. The article says: To seek the truth – the purpose and meaning of life.
To rest for most of the day
Not quite. The article says: To seek the truth – the purpose and meaning of life.
questions.rationale: “The conscious mind is free to involve itself largely in the great quest for truth, which should be the prime goal of every human being.”

questions.q: A new believer left after learning only two verses: “Whoever has done the smallest particle of good will see it; whoever has done the smallest particle of evil will see it.” Why did he feel this was enough?
options: He had been told to learn nothing more
Not quite. The article says: They told him every deed is accountable to God, which kept him constantly on guard.
He was in a hurry to return home
Not quite. The article says: They told him every deed is accountable to God, which kept him constantly on guard.
They told him every deed is accountable to God, which kept him constantly on guard
Well read. A self-correcting mechanism within.
They were the shortest verses to memorise
Not quite. The article says: They told him every deed is accountable to God, which kept him constantly on guard.
questions.rationale: “These verses tell us that man is accountable to God and every deed of man will be evaluated by God. Now I always keep this in mind.”
